bug_semantics: llama-server --sleep-idle-seconds unloads the model by calling server_context_impl::destroy(), which llama_init.reset()s the unique_ptr that owns llama_model (and the embedded llama_vocab) and nulls ctx/model (later ctx_tgt/model_tgt) but leaves the cached const llama_vocab *vocab member dangling. HTTP workers call wait_until_no_sleep(), observe !sleeping, drop mutex_tasks, then tokenize through ctx_server.vocab; the main loop can should_sleep() and destroy() in that window. Cyera's ASAN trace is free in destroy() on the main thread and use in tokenize_mixed / llm_tokenizer_spm_session on a worker; reclaim of the ~17816-byte model via /v1/messages or /completion yields a controlled load from vocab.pimpl (CVE-2026-43631). Tokenization endpoints that bypass the task queue are the sibling CVE-2026-43632, same sink.
flaw_origin: Idle sleep landed in ggml-org/llama.cpp PR #18228 (ngxson). Member e1d7b434 first wrote wait_until_no_sleep() with no in-flight handler refcount; 197e5785 first wrote destroy() that only mtmd_free'd mctx and did not free llama_init, so vocab was still live. e6ab62c4 ('make sure to free llama_init') is the smallest public first-write of llama_init.reset(); ctx = nullptr; model = nullptr; inside destroy() without vocab = nullptr — that is the dangling-vocab UAF. Same-PR 105e2f3c titled 'fix use-after-free' only moved metrics.init() across resume and did not touch vocab or the wait/sleep race. GitHub squash-merged the PR as ddcb75dd = tag b7492, the advisory floor. Cursor Co-Authored-By trailers exist only on later third-party patch commits in this patches repo and do not attribute the BIC.

reasoning: CVE-2026-43631 is a real, published use-after-free: sleep teardown frees the model while HTTP workers still tokenize through a non-nulled ctx_server.vocab pointer, reachable only with --sleep-idle-seconds enabled. Vulnerability-first search starts at Cyera's cited introducer (PR #18228 / ddcb75dd / b7492), not at Cursor trailers in the patches repo. ddcb75dd is a GitHub squash aggregate (one parent, message lists the 14 members), so it is not the BIC. Public PR members remain on GitHub; the smallest first-write of the flawed free is e6ab62c4, whose parent 44a5a26c still has a destroy() that does not call llama_init.reset() — verified by git show of both trees. e1d7b434 and 197e5785 are necessary setup (wait without refcount; destroy skeleton) but are not themselves the UAF. Same-PR 105e2f3c does not remediate this sink. AI judgment is BIC-object only: human author ngxson / Xuan Son Nguyen, empty trailers, non-bot committer; Cursor Co-Authored-By on 7c8f244a and later patch-repo commits is AI-only-on-fix and is ignored. No upstream fix SHA exists: #24063 was closed unmerged and HEAD 3173a564 (2026-08-29) still has the dangling vocab and uncounted wait_until_no_sleep race, so the finding is closed NOT_AI and unpatched.

unpatched.reason: ggml-org/llama.cpp maintainers closed GHSA-wwh3-vwx5-j8m7 and public PR #24063 without merging. Cyera's 2026-06-01 re-check on b9445 and this audit of HEAD 3173a56471c1753650cd806694145ffd6dcace67 (2026-08-29) still show destroy() calling llama_init.reset() without nulling vocab, and wait_until_no_sleep() still has no active-handler refcount.

potential_fix.approach: Increment an atomic n_active_requests in wait_until_no_sleep() and decrement it from server_res_generator's destructor so start_loop() cannot enter sleep while HTTP workers still use ctx_server.vocab; also set vocab = nullptr in destroy() after llama_init.reset() and fail tokenize/count_tokens paths when vocab is null.
potential_fix.rationale: The UAF is a TOCTOU between wait_until_no_sleep() dropping mutex_tasks and destroy() freeing the model that vocab aliases. A live-handler refcount removes the race window; nulling vocab turns a dangling dereference into a null check at the tokenize sink.
